::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[Is There A Way To Calculate Expected value From Variance And Vice Versa?](https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/1359640/is-there-a-way-to-calculate-expected-value-from-variance-and-vice-versa), asked by [gbox](https://math.stackexchange.com/users/103441/gbox) on Mathematics Stack Exchange (2015-07-13; [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)):

> If I am given the value of one (just the value), can I calculate the value of the other?
:::

Let $a > 0$ and let $X_a$ be the discrete random variable with $P(X_a = a) = 1/2$ and $P(X_a = -a) = 1/2$.  Then
$$\begin{align*}
    E(X_a) &= 0 \\
    \operatorname{Var}(X_a) &= a^2
\end{align*}$$

Also, as David points out in the comments, adding a constant to a variable changes the expected value but not the variance.  So these two statistics are independent.
